newsitem.title: FRANCE: French far right looks to ally with new party.
newsitem.headline: French far right looks to ally with new party.

text.p: A leading member of France's far-right National Front said on Monday his party was looking to an alliance with a new conservative party that he said was bound to emerge from the mainstream right-wing parties' stinging election defeat.
"The (Gaullist) RPR and (centrist) UDF are dooomed and discredited. They failed miserably," Bruno Megret, the number two in the anti-immigrant Front told France Inter radio.
"New parties must emerge, and one of them must accept the National Front as its partner," he said. "We agree to an alliance with the partners that are bound to emerge from the smouldering ruins."
All mainstream parties have kept the Front at arm's length, refusing to ally with it.
"If they had realised that there was an absolute majority on the right if it included the National Front, they would still be in power," Megret said.
A Socialist-Communist-Greens alliance ousted the ruling RPR-UDF coalition in Sunday's election.
The National Front won only one seat despite polling nearly 15 percent of the vote in the first round. Megret was defeated in his own constituency.
